earlier_scan.source_named: Salomon, R., Allchin, F. R. & Barnard, M. 1999. Ancient Buddhist Scrolls from Gandhara: The British Library Kharosthi Fragments (phonology of Gandhari, plausibly incl. accent); not open online

sources.citation: Baums, Stefan. 2009. A Gāndhārī Commentary on Early Buddhist Verses: British Library Kharoṣṭhī Fragments 7, 9, 13 and 18. PhD dissertation, University of Washington. xxxiv+709 pp. (Ch. 4 'Orthography and Phonology', pp. 110–199; Ch. 5 Morphology, pp. 201–239)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on the position of word stress. The 90-page phonology chapter has no accent/prosody subsection; a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/prosod yields only §4.2.1.4 'two moras of prosodic weight' (p. 121), §4.2.1.6 reduction of final vowels (pp. 125–128, discussing Fussman 1989 without invoking stress) and §4.3.3 (p. 191) 'Seven Old Indo-Aryan enclitic (unaccented) words have descendants in our text'.

sources.citation: Schlosser, Andrea. 2022. Three Early Mahāyāna Treatises from Gandhāra: Bajaur Kharoṣṭhī Fragments 4, 6, and 11. Gandhāran Buddhist Texts 7. Seattle: University of Washington Press (open access, OAPEN 20.500.12657/75824).
sources.note: Nothing on stress (a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/prosod: only ordinary-language 'stressed', 'distress').

sources.citation: Salomon, Richard. 2018. The Buddhist Literature of Ancient Gandhāra: An Introduction with Selected Translations. Somerville, MA: Wisdom.
sources.note: Nothing on stress (a full-text search for stress/accent).

sources.citation: Baums, Stefan. n.d. [online]. Outline of Gāndhārī Grammar. gandhari.org (abridgement of Baums 2009: 110–239; 'a comprehensive reference grammar by the present author is under preparation')
sources.note: Sound inventory and OIA>Gāndhārī sound changes (monophthongization, vocalization of r̥, Law of Two Moras, consonant weakening); no word-stress statement. The only 'accent' hit is the recommendation to transliterate the postconsonantal-v diacritic 'as a circumflex accent'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Gandhari language' (accessed 2026-09-17), citing Salomon, Allchin & Barnard 1999: 110 and Masica 1993 for phonology
sources.note: Phonology paragraph (three sibilants preserved, cluster retention, intervocalic weakening); no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Brough, John. 1962. The Gāndhārī Dharmapada. London Oriental Series 7. London: Oxford University Press. (Introduction incl. Phonology §§)
sources.note: scanned text (archive.org user upload) a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/penult/tonic/Betonung/an earlier reading: no statement on Gāndhārī word stress; only §73 'preservation of the written accent' (Vedic pada-text) and 'penultimate syllable' in text-critical notes.

sources.citation: Burrow, T. 1937. The Language of the Kharoṣṭhi Documents from Chinese Turkestan. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. (Niya Prakrit; Phonology §§1–33)
sources.note: No stress rule. Incidental: 'As unaccented forms their initial would be liable to be treated as intervocalic t, i.e. become voiced' (p. 6, pronominal forms); s in unaccented particles treated as intervocalic (p. 9); se 'voiced owing to its being unaccented' (§80); 'the liability of k to be dropped in certain positions of weak stress cf. §16'; samaho 'weakly stressed' (p. 43).

sources.citation: Konow, Sten (ed.). 1929. Kharoshṭhī Inscriptions with the Exception of Those of Aśoka. Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum II.1. Calcutta: Government of India. (Introduction, Phonology pp. c–cxiii)
sources.note: No stress rule. Two incidental mentions: aya de (Skr. ayam te) 'where m in the enclitic te is treated as belonging to the accented word' (p. civ); 'The v-sound, however, seems to have been little pronounced in unaccented terminations' (p. cvii, on gerunds).

sources.citation: Mitra, Sailendranath & Barua, B. M. 1921. Prakrit Dhammapada, based upon M. Senart's Kharoṣṭhī Manuscript. Calcutta: University of Calcutta.
sources.note: Nothing on stress (a full-text search for stress/accent: only 'accentuate' in the ordinary sense).

tone.summary: Short encyclopaedia sketch; phonology paragraph is purely segmental/historical (sibilants, clusters, intervocalic weakening). Nothing on tone, accent or word stress.

sources.note: The fullest phonological interpretation of Gāndhārī spelling as a spoken language; proposes merger of all final vowels to short [ə] and a three-way syllable typology (Baums 2009: 125–127), the material from which a stress rule, if anyone has stated one for Gāndhārī, would come.
